title: Region-selection rubric + harm-scan checklist
context: open-data-explainers fans into per-region tasks (one county, one metro, one area). Without a principled rubric, region selection can cherry-pick areas to tell a particular story, introduce geographic bias, or inadvertently stigmatise communities — especially for place-level modules like transit-access, amenities, and collision-hotspots. A region rubric and harm-scan checklist ensure regions are chosen by need and data coverage, not by the narrative they support.
objective: Define the region-selection rubric (criteria for choosing regions for new explainer tasks) and the harm-scan checklist (for place-level explainers) to prevent cherry-picking bias and place-level stigmatisation.
acceptanceCriteria: Region-selection rubric specifies criteria for choosing regions: data availability, community need or coverage, and a prohibition on cherry-picking areas to support a pre-determined story.

Harm-scan checklist covers at minimum: could this explainer stigmatise a neighbourhood or community, read as redlining-adjacent, enable targeting or profiling, or be mistaken for a recommendation/ranking of places?
Rubric and checklist are concise and actionable for a non-expert contributor pulling a task.
resources: PLAN.md — Goals and non-goals section (region-selection rubric goal)
PLAN.md — Quality, review & risk gates section (harm scan gate)
output: A committed region-selection rubric + harm-scan checklist document (e.g. REGION-RUBRIC.md), referenced by every per-region task as a prerequisite for region selection.
